meta.titre: Impact of World War One on Africa: soldiers, carriers and new ideas
meta.sous_theme: Africans in the First World War and the effects of the war on Africa
tags: impact of world war one on africa

sections.contenu_markdown: Cameroon's own history was changed by the First World War: German rule ended and the territory was shared between two European powers. The war was fought in Africa as well as in Europe. Africans served as soldiers and carriers, and farmers had to supply food and raw materials for the war effort. The GCE returns to this theme because it joins two big ideas: what Africans did in the war, and how the war changed Africa afterwards.

items: The First World War was fought from 1914 to 1918, and Germany was among the defeated powers.
Before the war, Britain, France, Germany, Portugal and other European states ruled most of Africa.
Colonial governments collected taxes and used African labour to run their territories.

sections.titre: What Africans did in the war and what the war changed
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Two questions, two answers

The *impact* of an event means the changes it caused. Examiners ask about this theme in two ways. The **role** question asks what Africans did during the war. The **effects** question asks what changed for Africa because of the war. Never mix the two.

### The role of Africans

| Role | What it meant |
|---|---|
| Soldiers | Africans were recruited, often by force, into colonial armies. They fought in Africa against German colonies, including Kamerun and Togoland, and some French colonial troops, such as Senegalese riflemen, fought in Europe. |
| Carriers | Where there were few roads or railways, very large numbers of men carried food, weapons and equipment on foot. Many died of disease and exhaustion. |
| Producers | Farmers and workers were made to supply food and raw materials needed by armies and by industries in Europe. |
| Helpers | Africans served as guides, interpreters, messengers and labourers. |

### The effects on Africa

- **Political.** Germany lost all its African colonies. Kamerun was divided between Britain and France, and the former German territories were placed under League of Nations mandates. Britain, France, Belgium and South Africa took them over.
- **Ex-servicemen.** Men who returned had seen Europeans fight and kill one another. They had learned military skills and met people from other lands. Many demanded respect, jobs and rights, and some joined nationalist protest.
- **Ideas.** The Allies spoke of self-determination for peoples. Educated Africans used this idea against colonial rule.
- **Economic and social.** Forced recruitment and requisitions caused hardship, trade was disturbed, and an influenza epidemic at the end of the war killed many people.

variantes.nom: Outline or state the role of Africans
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is outline, state or list and the focus is on what Africans did.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write short, separate points, one for each mark: soldiers, carriers, producers of food and raw materials, guides and interpreters. Add a few words of detail to each point, but do not describe the effects of the war.

variantes.nom: Identify the group linked to nationalism
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a short question asks which group of Africans gained most from the war experience.
variantes.contenu_markdown: The group most often linked to later nationalism is the **ex-servicemen** (war veterans). Their war experience gave them confidence, and many became critics of colonial rule when they returned home.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Explain how the First World War helped to awaken nationalism among Africans.

[6 marks]

etapes.justification: Explain means give reasons and show how each reason led to the result, so every point needs a link word such as because or so.
etapes.resultat_markdown: I must give reasons, not just a list.

etapes.justification: Six marks suggest about three developed points: ex-servicemen, new ideas, a weakened image of Europe.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: (1) ex-servicemen, (2) ideas of self-determination, (3) the image of Europe.

etapes.justification: A point earns marks when it has a fact and a result.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Africans who fought saw Europeans killing each other, so they stopped seeing Europeans as superior.

etapes.action: Develop the second and third reasons.
etapes.justification: Each reason must show the link to nationalism.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The Allied talk of self-determination gave educated Africans a strong argument. Ex-servicemen returned with skills and confidence and demanded rights.

etapes.justification: A one-sentence conclusion shows that you answered the question.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The war did not give independence, but it gave Africans ideas and leaders for later protest.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** The war awakened nationalism in three ways. First, African soldiers and carriers saw Europeans fighting and killing one another, so the belief that Europeans were superior was weakened. Second, the Allies spoke of self-determination, and educated Africans used this idea to argue against colonial rule. Third, ex-servicemen returned with military skills, wider experience and confidence, and many demanded jobs and rights. In this way the war planted ideas and produced leaders on which later nationalism was built.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the First World War was fought only by Europeans.
items.pourquoi_faux: Africans served in large numbers as soldiers and carriers, and the war was fought on African soil too.
items.correction_markdown: Say that Africans fought in Africa and in Europe, and carried supplies.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing the loss of the German colonies when the question asks for the role of Africans.
items.pourquoi_faux: The loss of colonies is an effect of the war, not something Africans did during it.
items.correction_markdown: Keep roles (soldiers, carriers, producers) and effects (loss of colonies, mandates, nationalism) in separate answers.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the war itself made Africa independent.
items.pourquoi_faux: Most African colonies became independent decades later. The war was one cause among several of the growth of nationalism.
items.correction_markdown: Say the war helped to awaken or strengthen nationalism, and name how.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that Kamerun was a British colony before the war.
items.pourquoi_faux: Kamerun was a German colony. After the war it was divided between Britain and France.
items.correction_markdown: Write: German Kamerun was divided between Britain and France and run as League mandates.

items.erreur_markdown: Using events of the Second World War, 1939 to 1945, as effects of the First World War.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two wars are separate topics with different dates, so marks are lost for events from the wrong war.
items.correction_markdown: Check the dates 1914 to 1918 before you write an effect.

items.enonce_markdown: State three tasks that Africans carried out for the colonial powers during the First World War.
items.solution_markdown: Award one mark for each of three of the following: serving as soldiers; carrying supplies as carriers; producing food and raw materials; working as guides, interpreters or messengers; labouring on military roads and camps. **Any three of these tasks.**

items.enonce_markdown: Explain two ways in which the First World War changed the political situation of Kamerun.
items.solution_markdown:
1. German rule ended, because the Allied forces defeated the Germans in the territory.
2. The territory was divided between Britain and France, and each ruled its share under a League of Nations mandate.

Award a mark for each correct change and a mark for the explanation. **German rule ended; the territory was shared between Britain and France as mandates.**

items.enonce_markdown: Assess the view that the First World War was a turning point in the growth of African nationalism.
items.solution_markdown:
**For:** ex-servicemen returned with confidence and skills; the Allied talk of self-determination gave educated Africans arguments; the war weakened the belief in European superiority.

**Against:** colonial powers kept firm control after 1918; some protest groups already existed before 1914; strong mass nationalism grew mainly in later decades, especially after the Second World War.

**Judgement:** the war was an important beginning that supplied ideas and leaders, but it was not by itself the decisive turning point. **A balanced judgement with evidence on both sides earns the top marks.**

items_markdown: Africans served as soldiers and carriers and produced food and raw materials during the war.
The war was fought in Africa too, and Germany lost all its African colonies.
Kamerun was divided between Britain and France and ruled as League mandates.
Ex-servicemen are the group most linked to later nationalism.
Keep roles and effects apart, and say that the war helped nationalism but did not by itself end colonial rule.
